items.title: Foundation, provenance and upstream adoption
items.work: Attach genuine upstream Git history, resolve six missing original binary assets, verify locked dependencies, establish independent public repository capability, reconcile full upstream adoption.
items.acceptance: History is demonstrably derived from upstream; all 217 original file obligations and 366 commits/461 versions receive reviewed outcomes; six assets and exact lockfile baseline verified; destination is independently verified.
items.owner: Repository owner for repository creation/settings; maintainer for local adoption and evidence.
items.closure: Every assigned requirement has executed evidence or a recorded owner-approved disposition; no source preservation or tree match alone closes behavior.

items.title: Source meaning, references and dated research
items.work: Review distinctive contracts across original mappings and source requirements; review 91 references, accept dated jurisdiction claims, and link source→requirement→fictional representation→behaviour→executed acceptance.
items.acceptance: Every source requirement has specific semantic review, validated reference dispositions and bidirectional executed implementation evidence; jurisdiction claims have dated accepted scope.
items.owner: Research and domain reviewers; jurisdiction acceptance requires accountable owner review.
items.closure: Enumeration, generated links, generic mechanics, text adaptations and fictional boundaries are not semantic sign-off.

items.title: Calling and communications fidelity
items.work: Complete original product-specific calling, routing, shared-line, tenant/federation, media, voicemail, messaging and supplier-timed porting contracts.
items.acceptance: Each distinctive assigned catalogue obligation has source-specific scenarios for valid outcomes, failure and recovery through shared dispatch, with inspected effective state and evidence.
items.closure: Shared analogues and bounded integration cases remain partial until each distinctive obligation is reviewed and accepted.

items.title: Workforce, channel and commercial fidelity
items.work: Complete specialist channel/workforce/BPO behaviours, full commercial support scope, offers, supplier relationships, contracts and recurring economics.
items.acceptance: Assigned profiles and obligations have independent actor/offer/entitlement/customer scope and tested lifecycle, valid/failing workflows, support ownership and typed billing where applicable.
items.closure: A generic role, offer or shared workflow is not a source-specific profile disposition.

items.title: Enterprise coexistence, lifecycle and ecosystem
items.work: Complete specialist product profiles, coexistence/change obligations, installed base, support scope, connectors and migration/recovery; obtain provider certification only through providers.
items.acceptance: Every assigned distinctive behaviour has scoped product/customer lifecycle, coexistence, failure/recovery and executed acceptance; any external certification is explicitly evidenced by provider.
items.closure: Synthetic hooks and integration-scope tests do not establish provider certification or full product parity.

items.title: Jurisdiction and public-sector obligations
items.work: Accept dated AU/US/JP/EU jurisdiction research and complete government/defence procurement, information-flow and continuity obligations.
items.acceptance: Each claim and procurement obligation has dated, scoped evidence and accountable review; runtime scenarios remain clearly fictional training rules unless separately approved.
items.closure: Boundary tests, regional labels and fictional exercises never imply legal approval or procurement eligibility.

items.title: Campaign, progression, source catalogue and adoption
items.work: Review every source catalogue entry, incident, progression predicate, SP/commercial economy and remaining source family; preserve source-linked humour; continue complete upstream adoption.
items.acceptance: All original rows and source-linked comparisons have distinct reviewed contracts and executed evidence or owner-approved dispositions; progression rewards are once-only; archive proposals remain separately governed.
items.closure: Bounded mechanics and selected issue exercises do not complete all 13 levels/19 goals or the full catalogue.

items.title: Full acceptance, operations and release
items.work: Complete exact full suite and gates; full scope acceptance before handoff; hosted CI/protections, owner-reviewed governance, dedicated API project with provider-enforced monthly budget, real browser/offline acceptance, MCP and endurance/performance automation, then Pages release.
items.acceptance: Full locked-dependency suite, all release gates, every acceptance input, actual stdio MCP, real-browser/offline/mobile/tab/reload flows, endurance/performance, hosted enforcement and Pages artifact pass on intended release inputs.
items.owner: Release coordinator; repository owner for hosting, policy, budget and publication.
items.closure: No stage closes from a stale summary or test count; readiness is independently evidenced; adaptation remains disabled until its separate governance prerequisites are met.

assignmentRules.unmatched: fail; add a reviewed family or explicit requirement assignment rather than silently using a catch-all
assignmentRules.multiSource: fail; generated requirements in this revision have one source each; revise the index if this contract changes
